shape_construction: Believable task-specific proportions, silhouettes, construction, joins and object anatomy. Generic boxes, disconnected pipes, floating parts and unclosed architectural gaps are substantive defects. Judge intended stylization, not polygon count.
materials: Appropriate authored material vocabulary, scale, surface differentiation and consistency. Default/checker surfaces, indiscriminate tiling and texture pasted over primitive geometry do not establish finish. Do not demand wear where not requested.
lighting: Exposure, readable surfaces, shadow depth, light/material relationships across all important zones. Burnt-out whites, persistent darkness, flat unreadable surfaces and pervasive glare lower quality even if objects exist.
composition: Spatial hierarchy, focal readability, coherent massing and purposeful distribution at overview, street/room and close scales. Empty space is not inherently bad; unjustified barren requested working or inhabited zones are.
detail: Meaningful task-specific equipment, furnishing and environmental detail at large/medium/small scales. Repeated colored boxes, labels and token props cannot stand in for differentiated functional objects or rich requested spaces.
style: Match the requested/reference visual language across all zones. Real environments require plausible construction and material treatment; voxel/game styles require intentional resolved abstraction. Do not penalize coherent low-poly/voxel design for not being photorealistic.
scene_coverage: Substantive realization of the public brief and reference scene extent, connected zones, context and principal architectural/environmental features. Judge the realized scene, not merely presence counts or labels. Avoid requiring identical camera or incidental photograph clutter.
functional_identity: Visible differentiation and credible furnishing of required functional areas and mechanisms. A named room with token objects is partial credit. Compare defining reference features when supplied. Do not infer actual interactive success from appearance.

formula: continuous quality anchored to visible completion; coverage and deviation retained separately as diagnostics

environment.criterion: Preserve the broad dirt street descending into the distance, with a dense storefront edge on the left and a more open right side.
Keep buildings predominantly one to two stories, with believable door, balcony, wagon and street proportions.
Frame the town with sparse trees, dry vegetation and distant hazy hills rather than an isolated architectural backdrop.
Match warm, low-angle daylight, long directional shadows, shaded porches and a softly clouded, atmospheric distance.

features.criterion: Large two-story rectangular timber frontage dominates the left foreground, with a tall flat parapet and projecting cornice.
A continuous upper balcony spans the frontage above a deeply shaded ground-floor porch.
Slender square posts support the balcony; closely spaced vertical balusters line its outer edge.
Upper doors and windows have projecting timber trim; broad sign panels occupy the wall and balcony face without requiring readable lettering.
Horizontal siding, decking and rails show faded gray-brown timber, uneven discoloration and worn edges.

targets.label: Dominant timber shop frontage and balcony

features.criterion: A narrow two-story frontage rises beside the large balcony building, with a tall decorative false front concealing a lower sloping roof.
The parapet has a heavy cap, raised end blocks and a row of recessed rectangular ornaments.
Two tall arched upper windows sit beneath a broad framed sign panel.
Pale weathered timber siding and trim contrast with the darker neighboring facade and roof.
A receding sequence of narrow commercial buildings steps down the street with varied facade heights.
Flat false fronts alternate with visible pitched roofs, parapet trim and occasional chimneys.
Porch awnings, posts, raised platforms and a farther upper balcony create layered edges along the street.
Muted tan and gray timber surfaces carry sun fading and weathering consistent with the foreground buildings.
The broad unpaved roadway slopes gently away and has irregular edges against raised wooden walks.
Shallow wheel ruts and overlapping tracks run along the direction of travel.
Boardwalk platforms and short stair runs bridge the height difference between storefront entrances and road.
Compacted brown earth mixes with loose dirt, scattered straw and darker worn patches.

targets.label: Sloping main street and boardwalk system

features.criterion: The foreground coach has a tall enclosed rectangular passenger body, a sloped rear luggage section and an elevated front driving seat.
Large rear wheels and smaller front wheels have thin rims, radial wooden spokes and prominent hubs.
Open side apertures reveal seating; framing, undercarriage and a light roof luggage rail remain visibly distinct.
The body combines worn burgundy panels, brown timber framing and restrained faded gold trim.
Tall timber utility poles recur along the street, with crossarms and sagging overhead wires.
Simple hitching rails and low fences punctuate the open street margins without enclosing the main route.
Sparse trees and layered mountain silhouettes remain visible beyond the thinning town buildings.
Dry verge vegetation and weathered unpainted wood share the street's subdued brown and gray palette.
